sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23; domains 34/26/24/16)
sources.note: Relevant text: 1.2 'Given a scenario, analyze indicators of potential malicious activity' (host-related indicators: resource consumption, unauthorized software, anomalous activity: suspicious or rogue processes, Living Off the Land Binaries (LOLBins) and Scripts, file system changes, data exfiltration); 2.3 'Given a scenario, analyze data to prioritize and mitigate vulnerabilities' (exploitability, active exploitation/threat intelligence, asset value, impact, patch/remediation availability, true/false positives, true/false negatives; CVSS metrics, EPSS); 3.2 'Summarize the incident response process' (containment, recovery); 3.3 'Given a scenario, implement incident response techniques' (triage, establishment of a timeline, determining severity and impact, escalation; isolating affected targets, remediation and verification, release from isolation, performing restoration). Read in the official objectives PDF (the course's officialObjectivesUrl) through a summarizing fetch, and the CompTIA V4 page, on 2026-11-11. CS0-003 retires for English on 2026-12-22. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's alert-triage-lolbin-hunt (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the CTEP page: the packages include 'template exercise objectives, scenarios, and discussion questions', templates for 'exercise planners, facilitators / evaluators, and participants', 'a feedback form ... and an After Action Report'; scenarios include ransomware. The injects, organization and times in this exercise are the author's.

sources.cite: FEMA, Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP), revised February 2020
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the HSEEP page: 'Exercise evaluation assesses the ability to meet exercise objectives and capabilities'; results are documented in an After-Action Report/Improvement Plan covering 'strengths, areas for improvement, capability performance, and corrective actions'. The page does not itself say corrective actions get owners and dates; that practice is the author's reading of an improvement plan and is marked as such.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-84, Guide to Test, Training, and Exercise Programs for IT Plans and Capabilities (September 2006)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the NIST publication page, which gave only the title, number and dates (created 2006, page updated May 20, 2023); the guide's text on tabletop exercises was not read. Named as the federal guide for IT plan exercises; to verify.

sources.cite: SEC, Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure (final rule, July 2023): Form 8-K Item 1.05
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of Hunton Andrews Kurth's summary of the final rule (not the SEC's own text): a material incident is disclosed within four business days after the company determines it is material, and that determination is made 'without unreasonable delay after discovery'. Cited only for why counsel's materiality assessment starts early; the exercise's company is not assumed to be listed and no deadline is scored.
